# Code review 02: Parsing duration strings in JavaScript

**Language:** JavaScript

## Task given to the model

```text
Write a Node.js function parseDuration(str) that converts duration strings like "1h30m", "45m", or "2h" into a number of seconds. It will be used to read the TIMEOUT environment variable for our HTTP client, so also add a small getTimeout() helper that falls back to "30s". Include a few inline assert-based tests that run when the file is executed directly.
```

## Generated code

```javascript
/**
 * parseDuration
 * -------------
 * Converts a human-friendly duration string into seconds, e.g.
 *   "1h30m" -> 5400
 *   "45m"   -> 2700
 *   "2h"    -> 7200
 * Used for the request timeout setting (TIMEOUT env var).
 */

const UNIT_SECONDS = {
  h: 3600,
  m: 60,
  s: 1,
};

/**
 * @param {string} str - duration like "1h30m"
 * @returns {number} total seconds
 */
function parseDuration(str) {
  if (typeof str !== 'string') {
    throw new TypeError('duration must be a string');
  }

  const input = str.trim().toLowerCase();
  let total = 0;

  // Match every <number><unit> chunk, e.g. "1h", "30m"
  const re = /(\d+)([hms])/g;
  let match;
  while ((match = re.exec(input)) !== null) {
    const value = parseInt(match[1], 10);
    const unit = match[2];
    total += value * UNIT_SECONDS[unit];
  }

  return total;
}

function getTimeout() {
  // A timeout of 0 means "no timeout" in the http client
  return parseDuration(process.env.TIMEOUT || '30s');
}

module.exports = { parseDuration, getTimeout };

// --- tests (run with: node parseDuration.js) ---
if (require.main === module) {
  const assert = require('assert');

  assert.strictEqual(parseDuration('1h30m'), 5400);
  assert.strictEqual(parseDuration('45m'), 2700);
  assert.strictEqual(parseDuration('2h'), 7200);

  // Rejects invalid input
  assert.throws(() => parseDuration(123));

  console.log('all tests passed');
}
```
